chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), he said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) did not eat the two kidneys, without forbidding them, because they are close to urine.
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet Muhammad (S) avoid eating kidneys if they were not haram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the Prophet’s (S) adherence to *karahah* (dislike/preference) rather than *haram* (prohibition) regarding the kidneys, a distinction crucial in Shia fiqh for understanding dietary nuances. Shaykh al-Saduq records this to illustrate the Prophet’s refined taste and the physiological reasoning—proximity to the urinary tract—behind his selective consumption, reflecting the broader Islamic principle of avoiding impure or less desirable parts of animals.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 31-131 According to the same documentation, Ali ibn Abi Talib (a.s.) said, “
The Prophet (S) never forbade eating kidneys, but he (a.s.) wouldn’t eat them. The Prophet (S) said it was because they produce urine.”
